messages:
maria chen: quick sync — thinking about a hybrid seed+manifest strategy for air-gapped installs. goal: minimize initial image transfer while allowing partial resume and safe rollbacks. thoughts? :seedling:

sam patel: +1. curious what you mean by 'partial resume' — are we talking chunk-level resume or manifest-driven diffs?

maria chen: chunk-level resume for large model blobs, manifest-first for metadata and verification. flow I sketched: 1) bootstrap manifest (signed) 2) lightweight seed image with critical runtime + verifier 3) request chunk index, pull required chunks prioritized by activation plan 4) background prefetch of noncritical chunks.

alex reid: sounds right. tradeoff is number of roundtrips vs transfer size. in bad networks extra roundtrips kill latency. maybe allow an option to include a compact chunk-pack with manifest for high-latency sites.

jess koh: also: need a clear compatibility contract. seed verifier must be able to accept both chunked and monolithic images across minor versions. otherwise upgrades become nightmare.

sam patel: +1 on compatibility. proposing a stable "bootstrap v1" manifest schema with fields: version, component list (with content hashes), activation-order, signatures. we can extend later but the verifier must ignore unknown fields.

maria chen: exact manifest snippet I used in the prototype:```json
{
  "bootstrap_version": "1",
  "components": [
    {"name": "runtime", "hash": "sha256:...", "size": 104857600, "role": "critical"},
    {"name": "model-weights", "hash": "sha256:...", "size": 2147483648, "role": "deferred", "chunks": 512}
  ],
  "signatures": ["sig1", "sig2"],
  "activation_plan": ["runtime","verifier","model-weights"]
}```

infra-bot: deploy-check: manifest must have at least one signature from a root key; verify chain stored in seed or fetched via separate signed root file.

jess koh: for rollout safety: mark certain chunks relocatable and prefer pulling them from local mirrors. and include an automatic fallback to earlier model-version chunks if some chunks fail verification (but only for non-critical components).

sam patel: question: where do we store chunk index? on manifest, or separate index file? manifest grows large if we embed per-chunk entries for huge models.

alex reid: keep manifest high-level and add a chunk-index file referenced by manifest. chunk-index is paginated so we can pull ranges. that supports resume and low-memory verifiers.

maria chen: yep. chunk-index reference in manifest + an explicit "index_paging_size" so verifier knows how many chunk descriptors to request per round.

ops-team: ops note: mirror/relay behavior needs to be explicit. we should allow operators to stage a local cache that will serve chunks via HTTP with sticky routing. also need TTL and eviction policy for model-chunk caches.

jess koh: eviction policy idea: LRU for non-critical chunks, pinned for active rollout versions, and a cold-storage marker for archived models (evictable after N days). add a size cap per node and a global quota per customer.

sam patel: security: always verify chunk hashes before writing to disk. Do not trust source headers for size. zero-trust.

maria chen: rollback flow: if activation fails, verifier should mark the attempted activation as bad and trigger a safe rollback that references previous activation manifest (also signed). must be able to start rollback without fetching the whole previous model if chunks are present in cache.

alex reid: operational trick: store a small reverse-index mapping activation -> chunk list checksum so rollback can compare cheaply.

infra-bot: reminder: ensure metrics for boot latency, rounds-to-activation, bytes-over-wire, and integrity-failure-rate. expose as Prometheus metrics.

jess koh: UX: add an admin command `redwoodctl bootstrap-status --activation <id>` that shows which chunks are pending/failed and recommended ops steps.

maria chen: next steps: I'll draft an RFC with: manifest v1 schema, chunk-index spec (paging & checksums), verifier bootstrap contract, cache eviction policy, and rollback primer. will include a short prototype script for index paging. planning to share by EOD Friday.

sam patel: sweet. happy to review — I'll focus on paging & retry heuristics.

alex reid: i can take cache/ops section. jess can you own rollback primer?

jess koh: yep. will add safety heuristics and examples for canary rollouts.

maria chen: thanks all. tagging folks who asked to be notified: @alex reid @jess koh @sam patel :thumbsup:

ops-team: noted, will prepare mirror deployment guide for testing.

maria chen: closing for now — will post RFC link here when ready. :rocket:
